concept.name: Simple moving average
concept.definition: The unweighted arithmetic mean of the last n observations (usually closing prices), recomputed each period as the window slides forward; the most basic trend-following overlay.
concept.intuition: A rolling average that smooths day-to-day noise so the underlying trend is easier to see. Every observation in the window counts equally.
concept.mechanics: Sum the last n prices and divide by n; each new bar drops the oldest point and adds the newest, so the average moves through time. Used to define trend direction, support/resistance zones, and as a building block for other indicators such as Bollinger Bands and MACD.
concept.formula: SMA(n) = (P_1 + P_2 + ... + P_n) / n, where P_i are the last n prices (usually closes) and n is the window length.
concept.failure_modes: It is a lagging, trend-following measure: the longer the window the greater the lag, and in sideways, trendless markets price crosses it repeatedly, producing whipsaws.
concept.misconceptions: A moving average does not predict future prices; it defines the current trend from past data. Nor is any single length (e.g. the 200-day) inherently significant beyond convention and self-reinforcing usage.
concept.example: Closes of 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 give a 5-day SMA of 13; when the next close is 16, the SMA becomes (12+13+14+15+16)/5 = 14.

citations.source: Moving Averages - Simple and Exponential | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
